decisions.reason: The source's top-or-side connector-access policy for the main and sensor boards is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The connector-access placement preference does not change the interboard connector types, pinouts, roles, or electrical interface.

The power board's vertical installation orientation is already recorded, while the new top-or-side connector policy belongs to the separate connector-access Requirement and does not alter the form-factor attributes.
Identifying the sensor, main, and power boards in their prototype arrangement does not change the existing board count or separate-board architecture.
The source's dimension-flexibility clause is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY, while its connector-access clause is represented by the connector-alignment Requirement.
The placement preference for accessible cables does not change the sensor-board connector inventory, connector types, signals, or total count.
Mechanical connector accessibility does not change standalone USB power activation, regulation, source selection, or powered loads.
The general cable-access preference does not necessarily change the panel-control connector inventory, signals, or on-board button policy.
The source does not change the NTC terminal, J_BAT assignment, or battery thermal-protection behavior.
The connector-access policy does not change the charge-status display method, charge LED interface, component values, or population states.
The mechanical placement preference does not alter BOM completeness, sourcing data, approved components, or assembly population requirements.
Connector accessibility does not change the DCDC1 voltage, current rating, rail role, or Schottky-drop compensation behavior.
